chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Butler's Swedish girlfriend and the jealous doorman with the knife
summary: A girlfriend from Sweden visited, and the hotel doorman chased an Englishman who walked her home; the recording was interrupted and resumed January 29, 1979.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Chitterson says that man knows I wasn't doing nothing wrong. All right, but keep playing and breaking the house up, everybody's feeling good and everything -- everybody's getting whatever they needed. So, well, I had a friend come in from Sweden. She come down there to visit me and so I was happy as I could be.

So it seems on the door, that man on the door, something like a concierge, watches that door and see who comes in and comes out, so my girlfriend she said, you can go visit and do what you wish to do, so she said, that English fellow, he's walking her home and I said "You can do/ well, it seems as though the English fellow walked her home one night and this man comes out of that compartment that he was in with a knife and that Englishman made it. That Englishman like to tore that street up.

So when I come home, the man was downstairs, he was trying to tell me what had happened and so he showed me, begged my pardon, "I'm sorry I didn't catch him, please forgive me. I didn't catch him. I'm sorry." So I didn't know exactly, so she told me, she said why does he want to kill the English-man. I said because he walked you home, he thought that
Englishman was trying to get something good around here, so you know, and everytime that I would go down there with her, the Englishman -- this man would be, (roaring)
This is January 29, 1979. 65 Second Avenue, Jacques Butler, third tape.
